text: What does 'canonicity' mean for a type theory?
choices: every type has at most one element
every closed term of a base type (e.g., ℕ) reduces to a constructor (a numeral)
all proofs of the same proposition are definitionally equal
the theory has a decision procedure for type checking
explanation: Canonicity: closed terms of ground types normalize to constructor forms. CCHM achieves canonicity, whereas Book HoTT with the univalence axiom does not (open problem).
